title: Constant rates in anisotropic noise
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product outcome space. For every outcome $x$, anisotropic noise with every coordinate rate equal to $\rho$ agrees with product spectral noise: $T_{(\rho,\ldots,\rho)}f(x)=T_\rho f(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces
Every atom mass is strictly positive
$f$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
$x$ is an outcome in the product space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Anisotropic noise with every coordinate rate equal to $\rho$ satisfies $T_{(\rho,\ldots,\rho)}f(x)=T_\rho f(x)$ for every $x\in\Omega$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $T_{\boldsymbol s}h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}(\prod_{i\in S}s_i)h_S$ for real coordinate rates $s_i$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
